title: Deep graph: 40 levels, each step equally hard
html:
Deep graph: 40 levels, each step equally hard

Question: On a graph 40 levels deep where every step is equally hard, how much money does each society need, and does traditional research fall further behind as the chain of work gets longer?

Answer: At budget 256: best OSO (α = 0.2, β = 1). Against traditional, clearly better on hardest level, knowledge found (bits), knowledge per unit of money and waste; no clear difference on targets solved, bounty value and ROI. At budget 512: best OSO (α = 0.8, β = 1). Against traditional, clearly better on hardest level, knowledge found (bits), knowledge per unit of money and waste; no clear difference on targets solved, bounty value and ROI. At budget 1024: best OSO (α = 0.8, β = 1). Against traditional, clearly better on hardest level, targets solved, bounty value, ROI, knowledge found (bits), knowledge per unit of money and waste. At budget 2048: best OSO (α = 0.2, β = 1). Against traditional, clearly better on hardest level, targets solved, bounty value, ROI, knowledge found (bits), knowledge per unit of money and waste. At budget 4096: best OSO (α = 0.8, β = 1). Against traditional, clearly better on hardest level, targets solved, bounty value, ROI, knowledge found (bits), knowledge per unit of money and waste. At budget 8192: best OSO (α = 0.2, β = 1). Against traditional, clearly better on hardest level, targets solved, bounty value, ROI, knowledge per unit of money, money to the main level and waste; no clear difference on knowledge found (bits). At budgets 16384–32768: best OSO (α = 0.8, β = 1). Against traditional, clearly better on ROI, knowledge per unit of money, money to the main level and waste; no clear difference on hardest level, targets solved, bounty value and knowledge found (bits). At budget 65536: best OSO (α = 0.8, β = 1). Against traditional, clearly better on ROI, knowledge found (bits), knowledge per unit of money, money to the main level and waste; no clear difference on hardest level, targets solved and bounty value. (Compared at each budget; 8 measures, a clear difference is more than 2.7 standard errors.)

Design (fixed before the run): compared five societies (traditional, OSO at α = 0.8 and 0.2, half-open, open without flow-back) × 9 budgets · held the same: a deep generated graph (40 levels × 4, 2 new bits per step), 12 identical agents, equal money, knowledge reward 1 per new bit, no validation · measure: all of hardest level, targets solved, bounty value, ROI, knowledge found (bits), knowledge per unit of money, money to the main level, waste · 30 runs per row.

Caveats:

  • A simulation with guessed parameters: it shows how the rules play out, not that they work.
Details

The simple model on a deep generated idea graph (40 levels × 4 ideas, 2 parents each; every idea adds exactly 2 new bits to what it inherits, so each step is equally hard at any depth; 2 bounties on the top level). Held fixed: 12 identical agents, equal money every round (f = 0), no flat mint, a knowledge reward of 1 per new bit flowing back with α, no validation.

Values are mean ± standard deviation over runs.
